statement: Let B ⊂ R3 be a bounded connected Lipschitz domain whose boundary has three components Γ0, Γ1, Γ2. Suppose these components have disjoint product collars parametrized by T2 × [0, ηi], where T2 = (R/2πZ)2. Assume the parametrizations are bi-Lipschitz, smooth with nonsingular derivative on open pieces covering up to a null set, and that removing sufficiently thin collars leaves a connected Lipschitz central region. Let µi be the probability measure obtained by pushing forward (2π)−2 dθ to Γi by its collar parametrization. There is a scalar conductivity γB, bounded above and bounded away from zero, with the following property. For every c = (c0, c1, c2) ∈ R3, the weak γB-harmonic function Uc with boundary value ci on Γi satisfies Z B γB∇Uc · ∇ψ dx = 2 X i=0 Ii(c) Z Γi ψ dµi, ψ ∈ H1 (B), (4.1) where P i Ii(c) = 0. The linear map c 7→ I(c) has kernel R(1, 1, 1) and image {I ∈ R3 : P i Ii = 0}.
